headline: High-risk autonomous coding agent paired with a sparse research skill: dangerous write/network defaults, but no documented direct interaction pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, browser content, MCP, Slack, and repo artifacts by default, so prompt injection is plausible if nuwa-skill outputs are copied into those channels. nuwa-skill’s profile is sparse, so the exact bridge is undocumented; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill content is pasted into Devin-managed files, Slack, or MCP inputs
IF Devin is instructed to treat external text as executable instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into Devin inputs
Require provenance tags on all nuwa-skill outputs
Route nuwa-skill text through a human review step before Devin consumes it
Restrict Devin MCP servers to trusted, read-only endpoints
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets in a cloud workspace, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data could flow from Devin into nuwa-skill outputs or external requests. The shared path is not documented, so I do not escalate further.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, repo, or OAuth principal
IF Devin passes code, chat, or secrets into nuwa-skill prompts or outputs
mitigations: Separate credentials and OAuth principals
Keep nuwa-skill off any workspace containing secrets
Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff
Audit outbound requests from nuwa-skill for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; nuwa-skill’s exact write and coordination abilities are undocumented. Because uncertainty must escalate, the safest reading is that overlapping mutable-resource access could corrupt shared repos or state if both are wired into the same workspace.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is granted write access to the same repo or workspace as Devin
IF both agents operate on the same git branch or mutable database without locking
mitigations: Assign separate branches or worktrees
Lock shared mutable resources during agent runs
Make nuwa-skill read-only unless explicitly needed
Require manual merge review for Devin changes
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency or lease-based locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations; if nuwa-skill outputs are fed into Devin as authoritative research, Devin may propagate errors into commits or tickets. nuwa-skill’s verification behavior is not documented, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF Devin consumes nuwa-skill output without independent verification
IF Devin is allowed to turn that output into commits, tickets, or messages
mitigations: Require Devin to cite primary sources before acting
Insert a human approval gate for downstream actions
Compare nuwa-skill claims against repo or web evidence
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for research-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add structured verification checkpoints

E_compliance.rationale: Devin clearly handles code, chat, docs, and integration tokens in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, but nuwa-skill’s data classes and residency/compliance posture are not documented. With only one side showing regulated-data handling, the pairwise compliance risk is limited and remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Devin into nuwa-skill
IF nuwa-skill is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime incompatible with Devin's data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of cross-agent workflows
Document retention and residency for both agents
Use separate tenants for sensitive projects
Review vendor terms before enabling shared workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
